artwork.abstract: The Pyramides at Port-Coton, Rough Sea is a series of six paintings produced by Claude Monet in 1886. They all show the rocky Atlantic coast of Belle-Île-en-Mer, visited and painted in the plein air by the artist between 12 September and 25 October that year.

prompt: Generate a square reproduction of an Impressionist seascape dominated by offshore rock formations. Place a tall narrow rock pillar slightly left of center, rising vertically from vivid blue water. Around it scatter smaller jagged rocks, especially to the right and lower foreground, with white surf churning among them. The sea should sparkle with dense, broken strokes of blue, turquoise, violet, and white, while the distant horizon is pale and lightly pink-lavender under a soft sky. Emphasize energetic impasto, crisp coastal light, and the textured aged surface of oil on canvas, with no modern sharpening or photographic realism.
